Held bounded positional read or streaming digest: original BigInt file fingerprint and every parent are checked before the first byte and after consumption; links, swaps, growth and close errors stop the operation. Streaming uses at most 64 KiB; existing allocation limits are unchanged. Independently re-reviewed with exact-bound, short-read, partial-final-chunk, FD 0 and substitution regressions.

Re-reviewed RC160: the journal path is a 64-hex token beneath a private bound root. lstat is followed by O_NOFOLLOW/O_NONBLOCK open and fstat regular-file, link-count and dev/ino validation; bytes are read through the held descriptor, then file and parent identities are rechecked. Changes fail closed; no checked path is reopened for content.
The flagged legacy header probe reads at most eight bytes from the held original BigInt object; post-check and caller workdir binding reject replacement.

The two regex replacements turn markdown-it output from fixed synthetic CSV/table fixtures into comparison-only visible text. They are not an HTML sanitizer or a browser sink, cannot authorize publication, and the product Markdown renderer does not use this test helper. This non-shipped helper constructs one deliberately legacy PDF Standard Security revision-2 fixture. MD5 and RC4 are mandated by that old PDF format solely to make a synthetic encrypted-PDF parser test; they are not used for user authentication, stored application passwords or DataSecure encryption.

Both reads are regression assertions against source fixtures created inside the test-owned isolated directory: one compares unchanged OCR/deferred-review bytes, the other compares unchanged XLSX bytes after processing. The tested product path uses separately bound input bytes; these test reads do not authorize a product read, write or export.

These six reads inspect mappings, private mapping text, generated Markdown and unchanged synthetic sources under the package smoke's exclusive temporary test tree. They assert the shipped sidecar's output and source preservation; none is used by the application to grant document approval, choose an export path or read user data.
